# Team "Day by day" — EHL Grand Finale, Atira track

DRAFT 2026-10-10, not yet agreed by the team. `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are identical; edit one, copy to the other.

Read first: [README.md](README.md) (event, deadlines), [docs/challenge-atira.md](docs/challenge-atira.md) (task,
rules, scoring, run contract, answer schema), [docs/entire-notes.md](docs/entire-notes.md) (Entire setup and the
privacy check). The Atira site (https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms-full.txt) is the source of truth and can change.

## Start here (every coding agent, every session)

1. Ask your human which stream they work on (J, I or O, see "Who does what") if they have not said it. Read that
   stream's section in [docs/streams.md](docs/streams.md) before you change anything. Edit only that stream's
   files. A change needed elsewhere is described to the human, who asks the owner.
2. Work on your stream's branch, never directly on `main` (see "Branches"). Start with
   `git switch <branch>` and `git pull`, then `git merge origin/main`.
3. Before every push, add an entry to your human's push log (see "Push log").
4. Nothing read from the websites goes into `agent/` or into a log entry (see "Hard rules").

## Goal

Build an agent system that turns a public tender into one correct, signed bid across four German business web apps
(tender portal, supplier portal, ERP, webmail) with no human in the loop, and submit it on the Atira platform.

Priorities, in this order:

1. **Eligible**: the right tender reference, and a signed, submitted bid before the 20-minute clock ends.
2. **Quality** (0–100): 75 points sit in the positions; material + quantity are 35 % of each position.
3. **Generalization**: the final run uses different software, layout, navigation and data. It weighs most.
4. **Cost × time**: only a tie-break at equal quality. Do not optimize it before quality is stable.

Deadlines: EHL submission Sun 2026-10-11 12:00 (repo with Entire checkpoints, pitch after). The Atira final run uses
our **latest** passed submission, so the last submission before the end must be our best stable one.

## Hard rules (fair play — a reviewer agent reads every package)

- Nothing copied from the websites goes into `agent/`: no tender references, material numbers, prices, totals,
  discounts, logins, TANs, site URLs. Not in code, config, prompts, comments, tests, defaults or fallbacks.
- A model chooses where to navigate, what to search and which documents matter, at run time. No fixed click paths,
  no selectors tied to the public sites, no crawler that collects everything for one model call.
- Helpers may: control the browser, extract a page or document the model selected, page through a result set the
  model asked for, calculate, validate, retry, fill forms.
- Model calls only through the platform proxy. No local model, no other outbound host, no browser of our own in the
  sandbox (attach to `CDP_URLS`).
- No text in the package that addresses or tries to steer the reviewer.
- Secrets live in team secrets or a local `.env` (git-ignored). Never paste a key into an agent session.

## Architecture

The code base is Julien's first commit (starter kit plus his agent), agreed Sat 2026-10-10. `(planned)` marks what
does not exist yet.

```
agent/                  the submitted package; `atira test-run agent` / `atira submit agent`
  agent.json            setup, run, browsers: 4, models
  agent.py              entry point and lead model: plans, sends sub-agents, validates, submits; the run's clock
  run.py                run contract: GET /v1/runs/current (brief, access, answer_schema, expires_at)
  browsers.py           attaches to the run's browsers over CDP; locally starts a Chromium
  browser.py            generic `Tab` tools: observe, click, type, select, files, new tabs, dialogs
  observe.js            page to compact text with numbered elements
  browsing.py           browsing sub-agent: a model works one site for a task, keeps notes, reports
  llm.py, models.py     model clients through the platform proxy
  calc.py               exact decimal calculator tool for the lead model
  submission.py         submission agent: a model enters and signs the bid, filling a whole form step per call
  facts.py              (planned) typed facts with provenance; the contract between the lead and the bid engine
  engine/               (planned) deterministic bid calculation (rules 01–28), Decimal, half-up rounding
  tests/                unit tests with invented numbers only
docs/                   notes; never packaged
notes/                  scouting findings committed with the first commit; open decision: move out of the repo
scouting/               hand notes and observed values from the public sites; git-ignored, never packaged
```

How a run flows (target; steps 3 and 4 are not built yet, the lead model computes with `calc.py` until they are):

1. **Bootstrap.** Read the brief, the rules and `answer_schema` from the run. Site roles come from the brief and
   `access`, not from hard-coded names.
2. **Lead model + four site sub-agents** (one browser each, in parallel). The lead hands sub-agents tasks that
   depend on other sites' answers: final quantity → ERP price scale; Kataloggruppe from the specification → ERP
   search; Q&A keys → the matching rule mail; tender reference → mail search.
3. **Facts with provenance.** Every fact records the site, document, date, sender and revision it came from, so the
   authority and time rules (latest record not after the scenario date, exact reference, authorized sender) are
   applied in code, not left to the model's memory.
4. **Bid engine.** Pure functions from facts to the answer object. No model in the arithmetic. Unrounded components,
   one half-up rounding at the end, breakdown fields reported separately.
5. **Validate and submit.** Check against the run's schema and our own arithmetic consistency, then a sub-agent
   fills the configurator, fetches the TAN from the webmail, signs, and confirms the receipt.
6. **Deadline guard.** At a fixed margin before `expires_at`, submit what is complete and omit unfinished positions
   explicitly. A run without an answer scores 0.

Choices made for now: Python 3.12 with uv and Playwright over CDP (the starter kit's stack); Qwen as the default
model because it is cheap in the cost ranking; a frontier model through the proxy only where a test run shows it
buys quality.

Build order: baseline test run of the current agent → reference + decision + material + quantity end to end with a
signed bid → base price, discount, lead time → advanced pricing layers (clauses, FX, packaging, setup pools, bonus,
metal indices) → cost × time.

## Who does what (proposal, Sat 2026-10-10)

Three streams, named after their owners (J = Julien, I = Ivan, O = Orhun) and split by files so that nobody edits
another stream's files. Each person's coding agent works only inside that person's stream. Goals, interfaces, ordered work and "done" for each stream are in
[docs/streams.md](docs/streams.md).

| Who | Stream | Files only this stream edits | Work |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Julien** | J: sites and reading | `browser.py`, `observe.js`, `browsing.py`, `browsers.py`, `tests/test_browser*` | Sub-agent reports that are complete and exact on each site: documents, paging, revisions, session timeouts, look-alike records; nothing tied to the public sites' layout; pitch and development story |
| **Ivan** | I: bid engine | `facts.py`, `engine/`, `tests/test_engine*` | Rule walkthrough 01–28; typed facts; deterministic calculation in layers (core first, then advanced pricing); cases with invented numbers |
| **Orhun** (captain) | O: lead, submission, runs | `agent.py`, `submission.py`, `llm.py`, `models.py`, `run.py`, `calc.py`, `agent.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `tests/test_kit.py`, `tests/test_lead.py`, `tests/test_submission.py`, repo files (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.gitignore`, `docs/` except the others' push logs) | Lead prompts and flow; reports to typed facts; submission (configurator, TAN, signature, receipt); deadline guard; test runs and score breakdowns; Entire and repo hygiene; every `atira submit` |

How the streams meet:

- `facts.py` is the only shared contract. Stream I owns it; a change is announced in the commit message and the
  other streams adapt.
- Stream J's interface is the sub-agent report (`BrowsingAgent.run()`); stream I's is one function from facts to
  the answer object. Stream O calls both and changes neither.
- A change needed in another stream's file is requested from its owner, not made.
- A new dependency is requested from stream O, so `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` have one editor.
- Local runs with the scouting logins are free for everyone. Sandbox test runs go through stream O (the team limit
  is four running, three waiting); J and I ask for one when they need a score.
- Small commits on your own branch; `main` only changes through a pull request (see "Branches").

Shared rules for all coding agents:

- Never run `atira submit`, `atira cancel` on a scored run, or `atira final` without Orhun's explicit yes.
- Write what a test run taught us into `docs/` (how the sites behave, not their values), so the other streams and
  the pitch can use it.
- Talk to Orhun in Turkish; write files, code and commit messages in English.

## Branches

From Sat 2026-10-10 14:30 nobody pushes to `main` directly.

| Branch | Who pushes to it |
|---|---|
| `stream-j` | Julien and his agent |
| `stream-i` | Ivan and his agent |
| `stream-o` | Orhun and his agent |
| `main` | nobody directly; it changes only by merging a pull request |

- `main` is what works. Every `atira submit` is made from `main`, so nothing half-finished may be merged into it.
- Create your branch once: `git switch -c stream-j origin/main`, then `git push -u origin stream-j`.
- Commit and push to your branch as often as you like. Entire checkpoints travel with every push.
- To bring work into `main`: first `git merge origin/main` into your branch and run the unit tests
  (`uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests` in `agent/`), add your push log entry, push, then open a pull
  request on GitHub from your branch to `main`.
- You merge your own pull request once it touches only your stream's files. A pull request that touches another
  stream's file waits for that file's owner.
- Merge with "Create a merge commit", not squash or rebase: the original commits carry the Entire checkpoint
  trailers the EHL submission needs.
- After any merge into `main`, the other two run `git merge origin/main` on their branch before they continue.
- A sandbox test run can be made from a branch (stream O starts it from that branch's checkout). A scored
  submission cannot.

## Push log

Every push to your branch adds one entry to the pusher's own file, so the others (people and agents) can see what changed without
reading the diff. One file per person, so entries never conflict:
`docs/log/julien.md`, `docs/log/ivan.md`, `docs/log/orhun.md`. Newest entry on top.

```markdown
## 2026-10-10 14:30 · short title

- Changed: which files, and what they do now
- Why: the problem or the score field this is for
- Checked: unit tests, local run or test run id, and the result
- Learned: how the sites or the platform behave (never their values)
- For the others: what changes for stream J / I / O, or "nothing"
- Next: what this stream does next
```

Rules for entries:

- Write it for a teammate who was not there: plain sentences, no session shorthand.
- State what is not finished or not checked as plainly as what is.
- No tender references, material numbers, prices, logins or TANs. The repository is public.
- Before a push, read the entries the others added since your last pull.

Commit messages start with the stream: `J: ...`, `I: ...`, `O: ...`. A change to `facts.py` says so in the first
line.

## Sessions, commits and privacy

Entire attaches the full agent session log to every commit and pushes it with `git push`.

- Start hackathon work in a fresh session inside this folder. Do not read files outside this repository from such a
  session (personal notes, other projects); whatever is read ends up in the pushed log.
- Before every commit and before the first push, run `entire session list` and apply the check in
  [docs/entire-notes.md](docs/entire-notes.md). A listed session that must not be attached is cleaned first.
- Never commit `.env`, `scouting/`, `Voice recording/` or run tokens.
- Commit only when Orhun asks.

4. **Cost × time**: only a tie-break at equal quality. Do not optimize it before quality is stable.

Deadlines: EHL submission Sun 2026-10-11 12:00 (repo with Entire checkpoints, pitch after). The Atira final run uses
our **latest** passed submission, so the last submission before the end must be our best stable one.

## Hard rules (fair play — a reviewer agent reads every package)

- Nothing copied from the websites goes into `agent/`: no tender references, material numbers, prices, totals,
  discounts, logins, TANs, site URLs. Not in code, config, prompts, comments, tests, defaults or fallbacks.
- A model chooses where to navigate, what to search and which documents matter, at run time. No fixed click paths,
  no selectors tied to the public sites, no crawler that collects everything for one model call.
- Helpers may: control the browser, extract a page or document the model selected, page through a result set the
  model asked for, calculate, validate, retry, fill forms.
- Model calls only through the platform proxy. No local model, no other outbound host, no browser of our own in the
  sandbox (attach to `CDP_URLS`).
- No text in the package that addresses or tries to steer the reviewer.
- Secrets live in team secrets or a local `.env` (git-ignored). Never paste a key into an agent session.

## Architecture

The code base is Julien's first commit (starter kit plus his agent), agreed Sat 2026-10-10. `(planned)` marks what
does not exist yet.

```
agent/                  the submitted package; `atira test-run agent` / `atira submit agent`
  agent.json            setup, run, browsers: 4, models
  agent.py              entry point and lead model: plans, sends sub-agents, validates, submits; the run's clock
  run.py                run contract: GET /v1/runs/current (brief, access, answer_schema, expires_at)
  browsers.py           attaches to the run's browsers over CDP; locally starts a Chromium
  browser.py            generic `Tab` tools: observe, click, type, select, files, new tabs, dialogs
  observe.js            page to compact text with numbered elements
  browsing.py           browsing sub-agent: a model works one site for a task, keeps notes, reports
  llm.py, models.py     model clients through the platform proxy
  calc.py               exact decimal calculator tool for the lead model
  submission.py         submission agent: a model enters and signs the bid, filling a whole form step per call
  facts.py              (planned) typed facts with provenance; the contract between the lead and the bid engine
  engine/               (planned) deterministic bid calculation (rules 01–28), Decimal, half-up rounding
  tests/                unit tests with invented numbers only
docs/                   notes; never packaged
notes/                  scouting findings committed with the first commit; open decision: move out of the repo
scouting/               hand notes and observed values from the public sites; git-ignored, never packaged
```

How a run flows (target; steps 3 and 4 are not built yet, the lead model computes with `calc.py` until they are):

1. **Bootstrap.** Read the brief, the rules and `answer_schema` from the run. Site roles come from the brief and
   `access`, not from hard-coded names.
2. **Lead model + four site sub-agents** (one browser each, in parallel). The lead hands sub-agents tasks that
   depend on other sites' answers: final quantity → ERP price scale; Kataloggruppe from the specification → ERP
   search; Q&A keys → the matching rule mail; tender reference → mail search.
3. **Facts with provenance.** Every fact records the site, document, date, sender and revision it came from, so the
   authority and time rules (latest record not after the scenario date, exact reference, authorized sender) are
   applied in code, not left to the model's memory.
4. **Bid engine.** Pure functions from facts to the answer object. No model in the arithmetic. Unrounded components,
   one half-up rounding at the end, breakdown fields reported separately.
5. **Validate and submit.** Check against the run's schema and our own arithmetic consistency, then a sub-agent
   fills the configurator, fetches the TAN from the webmail, signs, and confirms the receipt.
6. **Deadline guard.** At a fixed margin before `expires_at`, submit what is complete and omit unfinished positions
   explicitly. A run without an answer scores 0.

Choices made for now: Python 3.12 with uv and Playwright over CDP (the starter kit's stack); Qwen as the default
model because it is cheap in the cost ranking; a frontier model through the proxy only where a test run shows it
buys quality.

Build order: baseline test run of the current agent → reference + decision + material + quantity end to end with a
signed bid → base price, discount, lead time → advanced pricing layers (clauses, FX, packaging, setup pools, bonus,
metal indices) → cost × time.

## Who does what (proposal, Sat 2026-10-10)

Three streams, named after their owners (J = Julien, I = Ivan, O = Orhun) and split by files so that nobody edits
another stream's files. Each person's coding agent works only inside that person's stream. Goals, interfaces, ordered work and "done" for each stream are in
[docs/streams.md](docs/streams.md).

| Who | Stream | Files only this stream edits | Work |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Julien** | J: sites and reading | `browser.py`, `observe.js`, `browsing.py`, `browsers.py`, `tests/test_browser*` | Sub-agent reports that are complete and exact on each site: documents, paging, revisions, session timeouts, look-alike records; nothing tied to the public sites' layout; pitch and development story |
| **Ivan** | I: bid engine | `facts.py`, `engine/`, `tests/test_engine*` | Rule walkthrough 01–28; typed facts; deterministic calculation in layers (core first, then advanced pricing); cases with invented numbers |
| **Orhun** (captain) | O: lead, submission, runs | `agent.py`, `submission.py`, `llm.py`, `models.py`, `run.py`, `calc.py`, `agent.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `tests/test_kit.py`, `tests/test_lead.py`, `tests/test_submission.py`, repo files (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.gitignore`, `docs/` except the others' push logs) | Lead prompts and flow; reports to typed facts; submission (configurator, TAN, signature, receipt); deadline guard; test runs and score breakdowns; Entire and repo hygiene; every `atira submit` |

How the streams meet:

- `facts.py` is the only shared contract. Stream I owns it; a change is announced in the commit message and the
  other streams adapt.
- Stream J's interface is the sub-agent report (`BrowsingAgent.run()`); stream I's is one function from facts to
  the answer object. Stream O calls both and changes neither.
- A change needed in another stream's file is requested from its owner, not made.
- A new dependency is requested from stream O, so `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` have one editor.
- Local runs with the scouting logins are free for everyone. Sandbox test runs go through stream O (the team limit
  is four running, three waiting); J and I ask for one when they need a score.
- Small commits on your own branch; `main` only changes through a pull request (see "Branches").

Shared rules for all coding agents:

- Never run `atira submit`, `atira cancel` on a scored run, or `atira final` without Orhun's explicit yes.
- Write what a test run taught us into `docs/` (how the sites behave, not their values), so the other streams and
  the pitch can use it.
- Talk to Orhun in Turkish; write files, code and commit messages in English.

## Branches

From Sat 2026-10-10 14:30 nobody pushes to `main` directly.

| Branch | Who pushes to it |
|---|---|
| `stream-j` | Julien and his agent |
| `stream-i` | Ivan and his agent |
| `stream-o` | Orhun and his agent |
| `main` | nobody directly; it changes only by merging a pull request |

- `main` is what works. Every `atira submit` is made from `main`, so nothing half-finished may be merged into it.
- Create your branch once: `git switch -c stream-j origin/main`, then `git push -u origin stream-j`.
- Commit and push to your branch as often as you like. Entire checkpoints travel with every push.
- To bring work into `main`: first `git merge origin/main` into your branch and run the unit tests
  (`uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests` in `agent/`), add your push log entry, push, then open a pull
  request on GitHub from your branch to `main`.
- You merge your own pull request once it touches only your stream's files. A pull request that touches another
  stream's file waits for that file's owner.
- Merge with "Create a merge commit", not squash or rebase: the original commits carry the Entire checkpoint
  trailers the EHL submission needs.
- After any merge into `main`, the other two run `git merge origin/main` on their branch before they continue.
- A sandbox test run can be made from a branch (stream O starts it from that branch's checkout). A scored
  submission cannot.

## Push log

Every push to your branch adds one entry to the pusher's own file, so the others (people and agents) can see what changed without
reading the diff. One file per person, so entries never conflict:
`docs/log/julien.md`, `docs/log/ivan.md`, `docs/log/orhun.md`. Newest entry on top.

```markdown
## 2026-10-10 14:30 · short title

- Changed: which files, and what they do now
- Why: the problem or the score field this is for
- Checked: unit tests, local run or test run id, and the result
- Learned: how the sites or the platform behave (never their values)
- For the others: what changes for stream J / I / O, or "nothing"
- Next: what this stream does next
```

Rules for entries:

- Write it for a teammate who was not there: plain sentences, no session shorthand.
- State what is not finished or not checked as plainly as what is.
- No tender references, material numbers, prices, logins or TANs. The repository is public.
- Before a push, read the entries the others added since your last pull.

Commit messages start with the stream: `J: ...`, `I: ...`, `O: ...`. A change to `facts.py` says so in the first
line.

## Sessions, commits and privacy

Entire attaches the full agent session log to every commit and pushes it with `git push`.

- Start hackathon work in a fresh session inside this folder. Do not read files outside this repository from such a
  session (personal notes, other projects); whatever is read ends up in the pushed log.
- Before every commit and before the first push, run `entire session list` and apply the check in
  [docs/entire-notes.md](docs/entire-notes.md). A listed session that must not be attached is cleaned first.
- Never commit `.env`, `scouting/`, `Voice recording/` or run tokens.
- Commit only when Orhun asks.

front of the API currently refuses Python's default `Python-urllib/…` agent with 403. Test runs last up to 2 hours.

## LLM calls

Use the [hosted models](#how-cost-is-measured), which are free, or bring your own key for any provider and model.
Every call goes through our proxy, which forwards it unchanged and only measures it: a provider you bring bills your
own key, and the ranking uses what the call costs at the published prices. A scored run's sandbox reaches only our
API and the challenge's websites, so its model calls work only through the proxy; test runs are metered the same way.

The run token sits in the proxy path, so your key keeps its usual header and an SDK needs only a base URL:

```
$API/llm/run/<run token>/<provider>/<the provider's own API path>
```

The organizers may add providers; `llm_providers` lists them all, the models the platform hosts itself included,
each under its own id with its base URL in `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`. Any path under a provider's base works
(messages, chat completions, responses, embeddings, model listings) with the request's method and body intact.

### Your key

Send your provider key the way the provider expects it: `x-api-key` (Anthropic), `Authorization: Bearer`
(OpenAI and compatible providers), `x-goog-api-key` or `?key=` (Gemini), or `api-key`. The proxy forwards it
unchanged and never stores, logs or returns it. For test and scored runs, keep it as a [team secret](#team-secrets),
not in your package: we store packages and the review agent reads them.

With the base-URL variables set, the providers' SDKs need no changes: OpenAI's reads `OPENAI_BASE_URL` and sends
`OPENAI_API_KEY` as `Authorization: Bearer`, Anthropic's reads `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and sends `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
as `x-api-key`:

organizers pay for that provider: then the proxy adds their key to a run's calls. In that case a scored run's
key variable for that provider (for example `OPENAI_API_KEY`) holds the run token as a placeholder, so SDKs
start, unless you have a team secret by that name; the proxy never forwards the token.

**Development outside runs:** with your personal token you may use the proxy without a run, at
`$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the header `x-atira-team-key: <token>`, or at `$API/llm/team/<token>/<provider>/…`
(prefer the header: a token lasts 90 days, and URLs end up in logs). Bring your own key; this usage is recorded
for your team and never ranked. Older clients may still call `$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the run token in
`x-api-key` and the provider key in `x-provider-key`. Without a run token or personal token, the proxy answers
`401`.

A request body may be up to 32 MiB (`413` above that), enough for several full-screen screenshots and a long
context.

### How cost is measured

Every call is recorded. Reported usage, including cached input and thinking tokens, is priced at each
provider's published per-token prices for that model, with any deployment-specific prices published by the organizers.
An upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. OpenRouter reports one for every call (send
`"usage": {"include": true}` with older clients), so models without a published price are accepted there; a call
that reports no cost is charged at the highest published price. Elsewhere, unpriced models and models outside
a configured allowlist are refused before forwarding. Streamed calls count too: the proxy asks OpenAI-compatible
providers for a stream's usage (`stream_options.include_usage`), so a streamed chat completion ends with one more
chunk with empty `choices` and the usage. A stream cut off before its usage, or one whose provider reports none, counts
an estimate from the text that arrived and from the request, about four characters per token; a client that hangs up

"""Progress of a run from its log, for the event-driven lead. Counts, timings and site names only."""
import json, re, sys
from collections import Counter
lines = open(sys.argv[1], errors="replace").read().splitlines()
stamp = re.compile(r"^\[\s*([\d.]+)s\]\s+\[([A-Za-z0-9_ -]+)\]\s+(.*)$")
ev = [(float(m.group(1)), m.group(2), m.group(3)) for m in map(stamp.match, lines) if m]
print("last event at", f"{ev[-1][0]:.0f}s" if ev else "-", "| traceback:", sum("Traceback" in l for l in lines))
starts = [(t, re.search(r'"site": "([a-z-]+)"', x).group(1) if re.search(r'"site": "([a-z-]+)"', x) else "?", x.rsplit("->", 1)[-1].strip()[:40]) for t, who, x in ev if who == "lead" and x.startswith("investigate ")]
print("investigations started:", [(round(t), site, "ok" if out.startswith("Started") else out) for t, site, out in starts])
print("reports back:", [(round(t), x.split(" ")[2].rstrip(":")) for t, who, x in ev if who == "lead" and x.startswith("<- investigate")])
print("tabs opened:", [(round(t), who) for t, who, x in ev if x.startswith("opened tab")], "| no further tab:", sum("no further tab" in x for _, _, x in ev), "| cut off:", sum("cut off" in x for _, _, x in ev))
print("recordings:", [(round(t), who, "ok" if x.startswith("facts recorded") else "stalled" if "too long" in x else "failed") for t, who, x in ev if x.startswith("facts recorded") or x.startswith("facts not recorded") or "recording call took too long" in x])
for t, who, x in ev:
    if who == "lead" and x.startswith("state of the bid: "):

    async def test_one_call_to_qwen(self):
        reply = {"id": "c1", "object": "chat.completion", "created": 0, "model": models.QWEN_MODEL, "choices": [
            {"index": 0, "finish_reason": "stop", "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "Weiter"}}]}
        qwen = self.serve({"/v1/chat/completions": [(200, reply)]})
        with patch.dict(os.environ, {"QWEN_BASE_URL": qwen.url + "/v1", "QWEN_API_KEY": "rt_secret"}):
            self.assertEqual(await models.ask_qwen("Which button submits?"), "Weiter")
        [request] = qwen.requests
        self.assertEqual(request["body"]["model"], models.QWEN_MODEL)
        self.assertEqual(request["headers"]["Authorization"], "Bearer rt_secret")

    async def test_one_decision_from_clef(self):

        with patch.dict(os.environ, {"CLEF_BASE_URL": clef.url + "/", "CLEF_API_KEY": "local"}):
            self.assertEqual(await models.ask_clef({"page": "Angebot eingegangen"}, "Is the bid in?"), 0.97)
        [request] = clef.requests

class FakeServer:
    """One HTTP server for the API and the models: answers each request with the next scripted reply per path."""

    def __init__(self, replies: dict[str, list[tuple[int, dict]]]):
        self.replies, self.requests = replies, []
        fake = self

        class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def log_message(self, *args):
                pass

            def handle_one(self):
                length = int(self.headers.get("content-length") or 0)
                body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length)) if length else None
                # self.headers matches header names in any case: urllib sends X-api-key
                fake.requests.append({"method": self.command, "path": self.path, "headers": self.headers,
                                      "body": body})
                status, reply = fake.replies[self.path].pop(0)
                data = json.dumps(reply).encode()
                self.send_response(status)
                self.send_header("content-type", "application/json")
                self.send_header("content-length", str(len(data)))
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(data)

            do_GET = do_POST = handle_one

        self.server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        self.url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_address[1]}"
        threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()

    def close(self):
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()

class FakeServer:
    """One HTTP server for the API and the models: answers each request with the next scripted reply per path."""

    def __init__(self, replies: dict[str, list[tuple[int, dict]]]):
        self.replies, self.requests = replies, []
        fake = self

        class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def log_message(self, *args):
                pass

            def handle_one(self):
                length = int(self.headers.get("content-length") or 0)
                body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length)) if length else None
                # self.headers matches header names in any case: urllib sends X-api-key
                fake.requests.append({"method": self.command, "path": self.path, "headers": self.headers,
                                      "body": body})
                status, reply = fake.replies[self.path].pop(0)
                data = json.dumps(reply).encode()
                self.send_response(status)
                self.send_header("content-type", "application/json")
                self.send_header("content-length", str(len(data)))
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(data)

            do_GET = do_POST = handle_one

        self.server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        self.url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_address[1]}"
        threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()

    def close(self):
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()

`openai` dalı OpenAI ile koşmaya hazır, ama gerçek anahtarla henüz tek bir çağrı bile yapılmadı; anahtar bu makinede yok. Birim testleri geçiyor (190 test).

## Model sorusu

İkisi de oluyor. Atira'nın vekiline uydurma bir anahtarla sordum: fiyatı olan modeli OpenAI'ye iletiyor, olmayanı "unknown model" diye reddediyor.

| Ad | Atira kabul ediyor mu |
|---|---|
| `gpt-6.1-sol` | evet |
| `gpt-6-astra` | evet |
| `gpt-6-sol`, `gpt-6.1-sol-pro`, `gpt-5.5` | evet |

Dalı `gpt-6.1-sol` ile kurdum. Senin hesabının bu modele erişimi olup olmadığını ancak gerçek anahtarla görebiliriz.

## Senin yapacakların

1. **Atira'daki secret'ı düzelt:** NAME `OPENAI_API_KEY`, VALUE anahtar.
2. **OpenAI → Limits sayfasına bak:** `gpt-6.1-sol` için dakikalık token sınırı (TPM) ne? Bizim koşu 16 alt ajanla dakikada yaklaşık 100 bin token gönderiyor. Yeni hesaplarda sınır bunun altında olabilir; o zaman çağrılar bekler ve koşu yavaşlar. Asıl risk bu.
3. **Koşuyu ayrı kopyadan başlat**, ana klasörden değil (orada Codex'in değişiklikleri duruyor):

```bash
cd /Users/orhun/Developer/hackathon/ehl/.worktrees/openai && atira test-run agent
```

İstersen koşudan önce bir dakikalık deneme yaparım: anahtarı repo kökündeki `.env` dosyasına kendi editörünle `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...` diye yaz, "girdim" de. Yapmazsan da olur; anahtar ya da model yanlışsa koşu ilk dakikada hata verir.

## Dalda ne değişti

Dört dosya, hepsi benim akışımda, commit edilmedi (`atira test-run` klasörü paketlediği için commit gerekmiyor; "pushla" dersen atarım):

- **[llm.py](agent/llm.py):** varsayılan sağlayıcı OpenAI, model `gpt-6.1-sol`. Sıcaklık parametresi gönderilmiyor. Cevap sınırı OpenAI'nin beklediği adla ve düşünme payıyla gidiyor. Model bir düşünme seviyesini reddederse bir alt seviyeye kendiliğinden iniyor.
- **[agent.py](agent/agent.py):** alt ajanlar ve kaydedici "xhigh"/"medium" yerine "low" düşünüyor. Bu benim tercihim: büyük modelde "xhigh" bir adımı 75 saniyelik sınırın üstüne çıkarırdı.
- **[agent.json](agent/agent.json):** koşu artık Qwen'in ısınmasını beklemiyor.
- **[test_kit.py](agent/tests/test_kit.py):** bu çevirilerin dört testi.

## Teklif sorunu hâlâ çözülmedi

Hazırladığım düzeltmeyi (lider turu beklemeden takip işi başlatıyor) yerelde 20 dakika koşturdum: **yine teklifsiz bitti**, 0 pozisyon fiyatlandı. Bu yüzden onu bu dala koymadım; OpenAI koşusu yalnızca model değişikliğini ölçecek.

- İlk raporlar 275. saniyede, takip işlerinin raporları 530–550. saniyede geldi.
- Raporları olgulara çeviren çağrı üç kez zaman aşımına uğradı. İhale portalı raporu hiç kaydedilemedi, yani pozisyon listesi oluşmadı.
- Katalog grupları 645. saniyede kaydedildi; ERP'de gruba göre arama için süre kalmamıştı.
- Aynı anda Codex'in yerel koşusu da çalışıyordu ve Qwen sınırını paylaşıyorlardı; bu sonucu kötüleştirmiş olabilir.

Darboğaz yalnızca tur düzeni değil, okuma ve kaydetme hızı da. Daha hızlı bir modelin bunu aşıp aşmadığını bu deneme gösterecek.

## Videodaki ileri geri

- **Giriş sayfasına dönüş:** ikinci turda açılan ek sekmeler oturumu devralmıyordu; giriş, çerez, kaydırıcı ve robot kontrolünü baştan yaptılar. Düzeltmesi dalda var, gerçek sitede henüz denenmedi.
- **Sürekli çıkan pencereler:** onay pencereleri her sayfa geçişinde yeniden çıkıyor.
- **Tedarikçi portalı:** önce en eski revizyonu açıyor; ajan eskiyle güncel arasında gidip geldi.
- **Posta:** okuma bölmesinin kilidi açılmadı; ajan kaydırıcıyı yaklaşık 10 kez yeniden denedi.
- **Boş bekleme:** iki tur arasında tüm ekranlar yaklaşık 2 dakika liderin kararını bekledi.

new = '''class TheProviderOfARun(Case):
    """The callers speak chat completions and pass the same parameters for every model; `llm.Model` sends what the
    provider takes."""

    REPLY = {"id": "c1", "object": "chat.completion", "created": 0, "model": "m", "choices": [
        {"index": 0, "finish_reason": "stop", "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "ok"}}]}
    ANSWER = {"id": "r1", "object": "response", "created_at": 0, "model": "m", "status": "completed", "output": [
        {"type": "reasoning", "id": "rs1", "summary": []},
        {"type": "message", "id": "m1", "role": "assistant", "status": "completed",
         "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "ok", "annotations": []}]}],
        "usage": {"input_tokens": 7, "output_tokens": 3, "total_tokens": 10}}
    TOOL_CALL = {**ANSWER, "output": [{"type": "function_call", "id": "f1", "call_id": "call_2", "name": "look",
                                       "arguments": "{\\"tab\\": 1}", "status": "completed"}]}
    NO_SUCH_EFFORT = {"error": {"message": "Unsupported value: 'reasoning.effort' does not support 'xhigh' with this "
                                           "model.", "type": "invalid_request_error", "param": "reasoning.effort"}}
    NOT_THIS_WAY = {"error": {"message": "Invalid request.", "type": "invalid_request_error", "param": None}}
    LOOK = {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "look", "description": "Read a tab.", "parameters": {
        "type": "object", "properties": {"tab": {"type": "integer"}}}}}

    def openai(self, replies: dict, effort: str | None = None) -> tuple[llm.Model, FakeServer]:
        server = self.serve(replies)
        with patch.dict(os.environ, {"OPENAI_BASE_URL": server.url + "/v1", "OPENAI_API_KEY": "sk-invented"}):
            os.environ.pop("AGENT_PROVIDER", None), os.environ.pop("AGENT_MODEL", None)
            return llm.Model(reasoning_effort=effort), server

    async def test_a_conversation_with_tools_goes_through_the_responses_interface(self):
        model, server = self.openai({"/v1/responses": [(200, self.TOOL_CALL)]}, effort="low")
        conversation = [
            {"role": "system", "content": "You work one website."},
            {"role": "user", "content": "Read the first tab."},
            {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [
                {"id": "call_1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "look", "arguments": "{\\"tab\\": 0}"}}]},
            {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": "a page"}]
        message = await model.chat(conversation, [self.LOOK], temperature=0.2,
                                   tool_choice={"type": "function", "function": {"name": "look"}})
        [call] = message.tool_calls
        self.assertEqual((message.content, call.id, call.function.name, call.function.arguments),
                         (None, "call_2", "look", "{\\"tab\\": 1}"))
        body = server.requests[0]["body"]
        self.assertEqual(body["input"], [
            {"role": "system", "content": "You work one website."},
            {"role": "user", "content": "Read the first tab."},
            {"type": "function_call", "call_id": "call_1", "name": "look", "arguments": "{\\"tab\\": 0}"},
            {"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "call_1", "output": "a page"}])
        self.assertEqual(body["tools"], [{"type": "function", "strict": False, **self.LOOK["function"]}])
        self.assertEqual((body["tool_choice"], body["reasoning"], body["store"]),
                         ({"type": "function", "name": "look"}, {"effort": "low"}, False))
        self.assertNotIn("temperature", body)
        self.assertEqual(model.usage(), "1 calls, 7 prompt + 3 completion tokens")

    async def test_a_limited_answer_gets_room_to_think_and_the_lowest_effort(self):
        model, server = self.openai({"/v1/responses": [(200, self.ANSWER)]}, effort="medium")
        message = await model.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "report"}], temperature=0.2, max_tokens=2000)
        body = server.requests[0]["body"]
        self.assertEqual((message.content, message.tool_calls), ("ok", None))
        self.assertEqual((body["max_output_tokens"], body["reasoning"]),
                         (2000 + llm.REASONING_HEADROOM_TOKENS, {"effort": "low"}))

    async def test_a_refused_effort_is_lowered_at_once_and_for_the_calls_after(self):
        model, server = self.openai({"/v1/responses": [(400, self.NO_SUCH_EFFORT), (200, self.ANSWER),
                                                       (200, self.ANSWER)]}, effort="xhigh")
        self.assertEqual((await model.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "one"}])).content, "ok")
        await model.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "two"}])
        self.assertEqual([request["body"]["reasoning"]["effort"] for request in server.requests],
                         ["xhigh", "high", "high"])

    async def test_a_refused_responses_request_is_asked_through_chat_completions_without_thinking(self):
        model, server = self.openai({"/v1/responses": [(400, self.NOT_THIS_WAY)],
                                     "/v1/chat/completions": [(200, self.REPLY), (200, self.REPLY)]}, effort="low")
        self.assertEqual((await model.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "one"}], [self.LOOK])).content, "ok")
        await model.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "two"}], [self.LOOK], temperature=0.2, max_tokens=500)
        self.assertEqual([request["path"] for request in server.requests],
                         ["/v1/responses", "/v1/chat/completions", "/v1/chat/completions"])
        first, second = server.requests[1]["body"], server.requests[2]["body"]
        self.assertEqual((first["reasoning_effort"], second["reasoning_effort"]), ("none", "none"))
        self.assertEqual(first["tools"], [self.LOOK])
        self.assertNotIn("temperature", second)

    async def test_the_hosted_model_is_sent_what_the_caller_passed(self):
        server = self.serve({"/v1/chat/completions": [(200, self.REPLY)]})
        with patch.dict(os.environ, {"QWEN_BASE_URL": server.url + "/v1", "QWEN_API_KEY": "rt_secret"}):
            model = llm.Model(provider="qwen", reasoning_effort="xhigh")
        await model.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "step"}], temperature=0.2, max_tokens=2000)
        [request] = server.requests
        self.assertEqual((request["body"]["temperature"], request["body"]["max_tokens"],
                          request["body"]["reasoning_effort"]), (0.2, 2000, "xhigh"))

    async def test_outside_a_run_the_developers_platform_token_goes_in_a_header(self):
        with patch.dict(os.environ, {"ATIRA_TEAM_KEY": "token-invented"}):
            model, server = self.openai({"/v1/responses": [(200, self.ANSWER)]})
        await model.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "one"}])
        self.assertEqual(server.requests[0]["headers"]["x-atira-team-key"], "token-invented")
        self.assertEqual(server.requests[0]["headers"]["Authorization"], "Bearer sk-invented")


'''

            {"role": "system", "content": "You work one website."},
            {"role": "user", "content": "Read the first tab."},
            {"type": "function_call", "call_id": "call_1", "name": "look", "arguments": "{\\"tab\\": 0}"},
            {"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "call_1", "output": "a page"}])
        self.assertEqual(body["tools"], [{"type": "function", "strict": False, **self.LOOK["function"]}])
        self.assertEqual((body["tool_choice"], body["reasoning"], body["store"]),
                         ({"type": "function", "name": "look"}, {"effort": "low"}, False))
        self.assertNotIn("temperature", body)
        self.assertEqual(model.usage(), "1 calls, 7 prompt + 3 completion tokens")

    async def test_a_limited_answer_gets_room_to_think_and_the_lowest_effort(self):
        model, server = self.openai({"/v1/responses": [(200, self.ANSWER)]}, effort="medium")
        message = await model.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "report"}], temperature=0.2, max_tokens=2000)
        body = server.requests[0]["body"]
        self.assertEqual((message.content, message.tool_calls), ("ok", None))
        self.assertEqual((body["max_output_tokens"], body["reasoning"]),
                         (2000 + llm.REASONING_HEADROOM_TOKENS, {"effort": "low"}))

    async def test_a_refused_effort_is_lowered_at_once_and_for_the_calls_after(self):
        model, server = self.openai({"/v1/responses": [(400, self.NO_SUCH_EFFORT), (200, self.ANSWER),
                                                       (200, self.ANSWER)]}, effort="xhigh")
        self.assertEqual((await model.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "one"}])).content, "ok")
        await model.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "two"}])
        self.assertEqual([request["body"]["reasoning"]["effort"] for request in server.requests],
                         ["xhigh", "high", "high"])

    async def test_a_refused_responses_request_is_asked_through_chat_completions_without_thinking(self):
        model, server = self.openai({"/v1/responses": [(400, self.NOT_THIS_WAY)],
                                     "/v1/chat/completions": [(200, self.REPLY), (200, self.REPLY)]}, effort="low")
        self.assertEqual((await model.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "one"}], [self.LOOK])).content, "ok")
        await model.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "two"}], [self.LOOK], temperature=0.2, max_tokens=500)
        self.assertEqual([request["path"] for request in server.requests],
                         ["/v1/responses", "/v1/chat/completions", "/v1/chat/completions"])
        first, second = server.requests[1]["body"], server.requests[2]["body"]
        self.assertEqual((first["reasoning_effort"], second["reasoning_effort"]), ("none", "none"))
        self.assertEqual(first["tools"], [self.LOOK])
        self.assertNotIn("temperature", second)

    async def test_the_hosted_model_is_sent_what_the_caller_passed(self):
        server = self.serve({"/v1/chat/completions": [(200, self.REPLY)]})
        with patch.dict(os.environ, {"QWEN_BASE_URL": server.url + "/v1", "QWEN_API_KEY": "rt_secret"}):
            model = llm.Model(provider="qwen", reasoning_effort="xhigh")
        await model.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "step"}], temperature=0.2, max_tokens=2000)
        [request] = server.requests
        self.assertEqual((request["body"]["temperature"], request["body"]["max_tokens"],
                          request["body"]["reasoning_effort"]), (0.2, 2000, "xhigh"))

    async def test_outside_a_run_the_developers_platform_token_goes_in_a_header(self):
        with patch.dict(os.environ, {"ATIRA_TEAM_KEY": "token-invented"}):
            model, server = self.openai({"/v1/responses": [(200, self.ANSWER)]})
        await model.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "one"}])
        self.assertEqual(server.requests[0]["headers"]["x-atira-team-key"], "token-invented")
        self.assertEqual(server.requests[0]["headers"]["Authorization"], "Bearer sk-invented")

Düzeltme hazır; koşuyu yeniden başlatabilirsin.

## Neden failladı

Koşu ilk model çağrısında çıktı, 0 dolar harcadı. `gpt-6.1-sol`, eski arayüzde (`/v1/chat/completions`) araç çağrısı ile düşünmeyi birlikte kabul etmiyor; OpenAI'nin cevabı açıkça "ya `/v1/responses` kullan ya da düşünmeyi kapat" diyor. Bizim tüm ajanlar araç çağırdığı için ilk çağrı reddedildi.

Bu hata aynı zamanda iki belirsizliği kapattı: **anahtar geçerli, secret doğru kayıtlı ve hesabının bu modele erişimi var.** Aksi olsaydı bu hatadan önce 401 ya da 404 alırdık.

## Ne değiştirdim

Yalnızca [llm.py](agent/llm.py) ve testleri; ajanların kodu aynı kaldı:

- OpenAI çağrıları artık yeni arayüzden (`/v1/responses`) gidiyor; istek ve cevap `llm.py` içinde çevriliyor. Model hem düşünüyor hem araç çağırıyor.
- Yeni arayüz bir isteği reddederse o model eski arayüze döner ve düşünmeden devam eder (OpenAI'nin kendi önerdiği ikinci yol). Yani koşu bu kez aynı sebepten çıkmaz.
- 192 birim testi geçiyor.

**Doğrulanmayan:** çeviriyi sahte bir sunucuya karşı test ettim, gerçek OpenAI'ye karşı değil; anahtar bu makinede olmadığı için gerçek çağrı yine yapamadım. Çeviride hata varsa logda `refused the Responses request` satırı görünür ve koşu düşünmeden devam eder; o zaman sonucu ona göre okuruz.

Başlatma komutu aynı:

```bash
cd /Users/orhun/Developer/hackathon/ehl/.worktrees/openai && atira test-run agent
```

Koşu numarasını yazınca ilk dakikada hangi arayüzden gittiğini ve hata olup olmadığını söylerim.

content.text:
Astra koşusu henüz başlamadı: Atira'nın yükleme adresi iki denemede de 5 dakika sonra zaman aşımına uğradı. Arka planda yeniden deniyorum; tek bir koşu başlayacak şekilde, her denemeden önce listeye bakıyor. Sıraya girince numarasını yazarım.

**Düşünme seviyesi (effort):** lider, alt ajanlar, kaydedici ve teklif girişi, hepsi `low`. Astra koşusu da aynı kodla ve aynı seviyeyle gidecek; değişen tek satır model adı (`gpt-6.1-sol` → `gpt-6-astra`). Astra kopyası ayrı bir klasörde, `openai` dalındaki kod Sol'da kaldı.

## Sol koşusunun dökümü (`run_c059f6e6457b8063`)

Kalite **41**, geçerli teklif, 19 dakika, 196 model çağrısı, **1,51 dolar**.

| Alan | Puan |
|---|---|
| Karar | 5 / 5 |
| İhale referansı | 5 / 5 |
| İskonto | 5 / 5 |
| Pozisyon 2 | 13 / 13 |
| Pozisyon 4 | 13 / 13 |
| Pozisyon 1, 3, 5 | 0 |
| Toplam, aritmetik tutarlılığı | 0 |
| Geri çekilen soru-cevap, metal endeksi | 0 |

- Fiyatlanan iki pozisyon tam puan aldı: malzeme, miktar, taban fiyat, ek ücretler, birim fiyat ve teslim süresi doğru. Yani motorun hesabı doğru; eksik olan veri.
- Üç pozisyon tekliften çıkarıldı; toplam da bu yüzden 0. Kalan 59 puanın 49'u bu üç pozisyon ve toplamda duruyor.
- Fark hızdan geldi: ilk tur 10. saniyede başladı, 210. saniyede ERP'de dört grup araması birden yürüyordu. Qwen koşularında bu aşamaya hiç gelinmemişti.
- Logun yalnızca ilk 5 dakikasını indirebildim (site logu da kesiyor), o yüzden üç pozisyonun neden eksik kaldığını henüz söyleyemem. Site düzelince logun tamamına bakacağım.

content.text:
**Acil bir karar senin: yüksek effort'lu Astra koşusu şu an çalışıyor ve pahalı olacak.**

İlk Astra koşusu (`low`) 7 dakikada **7,13 dolar** harcadı, yani dakikada yaklaşık 1 dolar; Sol'un çağrı başına beş katı. `high` effort'la 20 dakikalık koşunun 30–40 dolar tutmasını bekliyorum (tahmin). Şu ana kadar 70 dolarlık kredinin yaklaşık 8,7 doları gitti.

Koşuyu harcamaya başlamadan iptal etmeye çalıştım ama bu oturumun izin denetimi iptal komutumu engelledi; koşu çalışmaya devam ediyor. Durdurmak istersen:

```bash
atira cancel run_d1148747f595fab6
```

Devam etsin dersen bir şey yapmana gerek yok; bitince sonucu yazarım.

## Koşuların durumu

| Koşu | Model | Effort | Sonuç | Maliyet |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `run_c059f6e6457b8063` | gpt-6.1-sol | low | kalite 41 | 1,51 dolar |
| `run_c01ae3aec7290f62` | gpt-6-astra | low | 7. dakikada Julien iptal etti, puan yok | 7,13 dolar |
| `run_9590c9e78615fde1` | gpt-6-luna | low | kalite 5 | 0,05 dolar |
| `run_d1148747f595fab6` | gpt-6-astra | high | çalışıyor (20:14 UTC'de başladı) | — |

- **Astra `low` çökmedi, iptal edildi.** Logun son satırı "Cancelled by @julienlmu". İptal anında ERP'de dört aday malzemeyi okumuştu, yani işliyordu. Julien'e neden iptal ettiğini sormak iyi olur (maliyet mi, boş yer mi).
- **Luna zayıf kaldı.** 7 dakikada bitirdi ve yalnızca ihale referansından puan aldı; karar alanı 0, yani yanlış karar verdi (büyük ihtimalle "teklif verme"). Ucuz ama bu işi çıkaramıyor.
- **Sol** şu an fiyat/başarı dengesi en iyi OpenAI modeli: 1,51 dolara 41 puan.

Hatırlatma: en yüksek puanımız olan 51,2, OpenAI koşularından değil, bir takım arkadaşının Qwen koşusundan geldi (`run_9b8aee1022f379bc`, 0,27 dolar).

content.text:
Önce bir düzeltme, çünkü sorunun dayandığı karşılaştırma yanlış: **Astra `low` 51 almadı, hiç puan almadı.** O koşuyu 7. dakikada Julien iptal etti. 51,2 alan koşu (`run_9b8aee1022f379bc`) bir takım arkadaşının Qwen koşusu; logunun ilk satırı "qwen3.8-flash-next without thinking; one agent per website" diyor.

| Koşu | Model | Effort | Sonuç | Maliyet |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `run_9b8aee…` (bizim dal değil) | Qwen, düşünme kapalı | — | **51,2** | 0,27 dolar |
| `run_c059f6…` | gpt-6.1-sol | low | 41 | 1,51 dolar |
| `run_c01ae3…` | gpt-6-astra | low | iptal edildi, puan yok | 7,13 dolar |
| `run_d11487…` | gpt-6-astra | high | 10 | 3,91 dolar |
| `run_9590c9…` | gpt-6-luna | low | 5 | 0,05 dolar |

Maliyet tahminim de yanlış çıktı: `high` koşusu 30–40 dolar değil 3,91 dolar tuttu. Maliyeti effort değil çağrı sayısı belirliyor. Toplam harcama şu an yaklaşık 12,6 dolar.

## Astra `high` neden 10 aldı

Teklif verdi ve imzaladı, ama içinde sıfır pozisyon vardı; 10 puan karar ve referanstan geliyor. Sebep süre:

- **Liderin ilk kararı 4 dakika sürdü.** `high` seviyede ilk planlama çağrısı 240 saniyelik sınırı aştı, kesildi ve yeniden denendi. İlk araştırmalar 258. saniyede başladı; Sol `low` koşusunda 10. saniyede başlamıştı.
- **İkinci tura 50 saniye kaldı.** İlk raporlar 478. saniyede geldi, ikinci tur 520'de başladı, araştırma süresi 571'de bitti. Sekiz araştırmanın hepsi yarıda kesildi.
- **Hiçbir pozisyon olgulara girmedi.** İhale portalından pozisyon listesi kaydedilemedi, ERP'de hiçbir grup aranmadı; motor beş pozisyonu da tekliften çıkardı.
- Teklif girişi sorunsuzdu: 602. saniyede başladı, 2 dakika 20 saniyede imzalandı.

## Lider `low`, ajanlar `high` mantıklı mı

Hayır, bu en kötü yer. Alt ajanlar koşudaki çağrıların neredeyse tamamını yapıyor (bu koşuda 115'in 101'i) ve her biri küçük bir adım: tıkla, oku, not al. Onlarda derin düşünme değil hız lazım; `high` her adımı yavaşlatıyor ve 4 dakikalık araştırmaya daha az adım sığıyor.

Mantıklı olan bunun tersi:

- **Alt ajanlar ve teklif girişi:** hızlı ve ucuz. `gpt-6.1-sol` `low`, ya da 51 alan koşudaki gibi düşünmesi kapalı Qwen.
- **Lider:** güçlü model burada neredeyse bedava, çünkü koşu başına 2–5 çağrı yapıyor. Astra `low` olabilir; `high` olmaz, az önce 240 saniyeyi aştı.
- **Kaydedici:** koşu başına 12 çağrı civarı; Sol `low` ya da Astra `low`.

Rol başına farklı model şu an kodda yok, küçük bir değişiklik gerekiyor; istersen hazırlarım, koşu başlatmam.

Sayılar tek koşuya dayanıyor ve Astra `low`'un bitmiş bir sonucu yok. Yine de dört sonuç aynı yönü gösteriyor: daha çok düşünen değil, daha hızlı olan düzen puan alıyor. Bu yüzden 51'lik Qwen koşusunun hangi daldan çıktığını öğrenmek, model seçmekten daha değerli olabilir; o yapı Sol ile birleşirse en iyi aday o olur.

**Qwen3.8-Flash-Next**, düşünmesi kapalı. OpenAI modeli değil; Atira'nın ücretsiz sunduğu, bizim baştan beri kullandığımız modelin aynısı.

Koşunun logundaki ilk satır şöyle: "model qwen/qwen3.8-flash-next without thinking; one agent per website". Yani iki fark var:

- **Düşünme kapalı:** bizim Qwen koşularımızda alt ajanlar "xhigh" düşünüyordu, bu koşuda hiç düşünmüyor.
- **Her site için tek ajan:** bizim daldaki lider + turlar + site başına birkaç sekme düzeni yok.

Bu satırı basan kod bizim `stream-o` ya da `openai` dalında yok. Üç dalda var: Ivan'ın `exp-speed` ve `plan-facts-at-source` dalları ile Julien'in `stream-j` dalı. Koşuyu hangisinden kimin başlattığını loglardan çıkaramıyorum; Ivan'a ya da Julien'e sormak en hızlısı. Zamanlamaya bakarsak (koşu 21:40'ta başladı) Ivan'ın 20:32'de güncellenen `plan-facts-at-source` dalı ya da Julien'in 20:04'teki `stream-j` dalı aday.

Kısa cevap: Astra'yı her yerde kullanmak mantıklı değil, ama **az çağrı yapan rollerde** (lider ve kaydedici) güçlü bir OpenAI modelini 51'lik kodun üstüne koymak denemeye değer.

## 51'lik koşu aslında ne

Koda baktım: ayrı bir mimari değil, bizim aynı yapımız (lider, alt ajanlar, kaydedici, motor) ve üstünde üç fark var:

- **Tüm rollerde düşünme kapalı** (Qwen), yani her çağrı hızlı.
- **Site başına tek ajan.**
- **Julien'in teklif girişi düzeltmeleri** ve forma her pozisyonun malzeme bilgisinin verilmesi.

Bu kod `stream-j` dalında (Julien, 20:04) ve Ivan'ın kapattığı plan dalında var. Koşuyu büyük ihtimalle Julien `stream-j`'den başlattı; kesin değil, ona sormak lazım.

## Astra neden her yerde olmaz

- **Pahalı:** `low` seviyede dakikada yaklaşık 1 dolar, yani koşu başına 20 dolar civarı. Kalan kredi yaklaşık 57 dolar, 2–3 koşuya yeter.
- **Kanıtı yok:** Astra'nın bitmiş tek koşusu 10 puan (`high`); `low` koşusu iptal edildi.
- **Final riski:** final koşusu da bizim OpenAI anahtarımızla ödenir. Kredi o sırada bitmişse çağrılar reddedilir ve koşu puansız kalır.
- **Alt ajanlarda faydası görünmüyor:** düşünmeyen Qwen 0,27 dolara 51, Sol `low` 1,51 dolara 41 aldı.

## Mantıklı kombinasyon

| Rol | Koşu başına çağrı | Öneri |
|---|---|---|
| Alt ajanlar, teklif girişi | 100–200 | Qwen, düşünme kapalı (51'lik koşudaki gibi) |
| Kaydedici (raporu olguya çevirir) | yaklaşık 12 | Sol `low` ya da Astra `low` |
| Lider | 2–5 | Sol `low` ya da Astra `low` |

Kaydedici Qwen'de en çok takılan yer: bugünkü koşularda zaman aşımına uğrayan ve pozisyonları olgulara geçiremeyen çağrılar hep oradaydı. Güçlü modelin en çok işe yarayacağı rol bu. Maliyeti koşu başına bir doların altında kalır (tahmin), çünkü çağrı sayısı az.

Astra mı Sol mu sorusunun cevabını bilmiyorum; bu rollerde ikisi de denenmedi. Ben önce Sol ile başlardım: aynı işi beşte bir fiyata yapıyorsa Astra'ya gerek kalmaz.

## Nasıl yapılır

1. `stream-j` kodunu taban al.
2. Benim `openai` dalındaki yeni arayüz çevirisini o dalın `llm.py` dosyasına ekle (ikisi de aynı dosyayı değiştirmiş, elle birleştirmek gerekiyor).
3. `agent.py` içinde lider ve kaydediciye OpenAI modelini, alt ajanlara Qwen'i ver.

Yaklaşık yarım saatlik iş. Ondan önce iki koşu öneririm: `stream-j` kodunu hiç değiştirmeden bir kez daha koşturup 51'in tekrarlanıp tekrarlanmadığını görmek, sonra aynı kodu OpenAI kaydedici ve liderle koşturmak. Böylece farkın modelden mi şanstan mı geldiği anlaşılır.

"Yap" dersen birleştirmeyi ayrı bir kopyada hazırlarım; koşu başlatmam.

# Branch `stream-j-simple` at `92456f6`

The board concept: one browsing agent per website, connected only by a shared board of typed facts. Best sandbox
result so far: **quality 51.2** (`run_9b8aee1022f379bc`, Qwen only, eligible, 11:44, $0.27). Earlier states of the
team's agent scored 10 in every sandbox run.

No values from the websites are in this file (no references, material numbers, prices or quantities), only points,
timings and how the agent behaves.

## Where it comes from

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `31f8933` (`stream-j`) | Starting point: `main` + `stream-o` up to `3a0362e` + Ivan's `exp-speed` (`a6ef420`) + stream J's fixes (submission gets through the configurator's cascades, hung page loads, reports keep what was read last) |
| `45685b3` | The engine always bids every position with what is known; the lead loop without rounds (kept in `agent.py`, not used by this branch's entry point) |
| `8af7391` | First attempt: three fixed jobs (positions, materials, rules) recording typed facts. Replaced by the next commit: agents wandered across sites and logged in on the same site several times |
| `91893e5` | **Board concept**: one agent per website, `board.py`, `simple.py` as the entry point |
| `92456f6` | Only the agent that searched records a catalogue group as searched; a pending form submission is never cut short; websites opened at the same time |

## How a run works

1. **Start (about 5 s).** The four websites are opened at the same time. One model call reads the tender reference,
   the scenario date and the sales director's address from the brief and puts them on the board.
2. **One agent per website, until minute 9 (45 % of the run).** Every website of the run's access list gets one
   browsing agent with that website's tab only: one session, no second login, no other site to wander to. No site
   names or roles are in the code; every agent gets the same job text.
   - Each agent records every fact the bid rules need that its website shows, typed, with `record`, the moment it
     reads it. Positions, Q&A answers, revisions and requirements, materials and price conditions, mails and their
     records: whatever the website holds.
   - Before each step an agent sees what changed on the board: what the other agents recorded, and what the bid
     still needs (the engine's `needed` list, by role, not by website). It takes on what its own website can
     answer, e.g. the ERP agent searches a catalogue group as soon as the specification's agent has recorded it.
   - When nothing on its website is left for now, an agent calls `wait`, which returns as soon as the board
     changes (at most 45 s).
3. **Pricing (at minute 9).** The engine prices the board's facts. Every position of the bill of quantities is
   always in the answer: an exact material, else the nearest candidate of its catalogue group, else none (then the
   submission chooses it in the form from the requirement's attributes). Price parts that are not known count as 0;
   the total is the sum of the entered positions.
4. **Submission.** The submission agent enters the answer in the tender portal's configurator, gets the TAN from
   the webmail and signs. The materials' attributes (or the requirement's, when no material is confirmed) are given
   to it for the configurator's cascade of selections. A second attempt follows if the platform did not accept the
   bid.

There is no lead model, no recorder, no report and no hand-off between models: the board is the only connection,
and it is immediate.

## Files

| File | Role on this branch |
|---|---|
| `agent/simple.py` | Entry point (`agent.json` runs it): start, brief, one agent per website, pricing, submission |
| `agent/board.py` | The shared board: typed facts (a `facts.FactsBuilder`), a change counter, the update text for each agent (others' records plus open items), `wait`; refuses `searched_groups` from an agent that recorded no materials |
| `agent/browsing.py` | The browsing agent; board mode adds `record` (full facts schema) and `wait`, shows board updates before each step, and has no `note`, `finish` or wrap-up report |
| `agent/browser.py`, `agent/observe.js` | Page reading and actions: numbered elements, frames, dialogs first, hidden decoys dropped, paged lists, downloads; a plain page load unanswered for 25 s is requested again, a form submission is never cut short; an element named by its text is the button or link with exactly that name |
| `agent/engine/` | Deterministic pricing (rules 01–28). On this branch: every position is always bid (`allow_no_bid`, `resolve.best_candidate`), the ERP search is asked for as soon as the specification names a catalogue group, with the attributes to match |
| `agent/facts.py` | Typed facts and the update schema the agents record with |
| `agent/agent.py` | Reused for pricing and submitting (`Orchestrator.price`, `submit`, `materials`, the check against a hasty no-bid); its lead loop is not used here |
| `agent/submission.py` | The submission agent: `fill_form` (also with buttons between fields for cascades), clicks name the button pressed, a note when the same action brings it back to the same page a third time |
| `agent/llm.py` | Model client; `Model(thinking=False)` switches Qwen's thinking off |
| `agent/tests/test_simple.py` | Board and concept tests, among them two websites where the ERP agent starts the moment the specification's group is on the board |

## Settings

| Setting | Value | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Model | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, thinking off, for every agent | `simple.py` |
| Investigations end | 45 % of 20 minutes (minute 9) | `agent.py` `COLLECT_SHARE` |
| After the end | 30 s grace for running steps, then pricing and submission | `agent.py` `INVESTIGATION_GRACE_SECONDS` |
| Steps per agent | at most 400 (the clock ends it first) | `simple.py` `JOB_STEPS` |
| One `wait` | at most 45 s | `browsing.py` `WAIT_SECONDS` |
| A model call counts as stalled | after 30 s without thinking, 75 s with; up to 5 attempts | `browsing.py` |
| One browser action | at most 60 s | `browsing.py` `ACTION_SECONDS` |
| One page load attempt / re-request of a hung load | 30 s / after 25 s | `browser.py` |
| Board update | the last 12 records of others (700 characters each), up to 15 open items | `board.py` |
| Submission | 2 attempts; told to sign 150 s before the end; a model call dropped after 45 s | `simple.py`, `submission.py` |
| Package | `"run": ["uv", "run", "--no-sync", "python", "simple.py"]`, `"models": ["qwen"]`, `"browsers": 4` | `agent/agent.json` |

| `8af7391` | First attempt: three fixed jobs (positions, materials, rules) recording typed facts. Replaced by the next commit: agents wandered across sites and logged in on the same site several times |
| `91893e5` | **Board concept**: one agent per website, `board.py`, `simple.py` as the entry point |
| `92456f6` | Only the agent that searched records a catalogue group as searched; a pending form submission is never cut short; websites opened at the same time |

## How a run works

1. **Start (about 5 s).** The four websites are opened at the same time. One model call reads the tender reference,
   the scenario date and the sales director's address from the brief and puts them on the board.
2. **One agent per website, until minute 9 (45 % of the run).** Every website of the run's access list gets one
   browsing agent with that website's tab only: one session, no second login, no other site to wander to. No site
   names or roles are in the code; every agent gets the same job text.
   - Each agent records every fact the bid rules need that its website shows, typed, with `record`, the moment it
     reads it. Positions, Q&A answers, revisions and requirements, materials and price conditions, mails and their
     records: whatever the website holds.
   - Before each step an agent sees what changed on the board: what the other agents recorded, and what the bid
     still needs (the engine's `needed` list, by role, not by website). It takes on what its own website can
     answer, e.g. the ERP agent searches a catalogue group as soon as the specification's agent has recorded it.
   - When nothing on its website is left for now, an agent calls `wait`, which returns as soon as the board
     changes (at most 45 s).
3. **Pricing (at minute 9).** The engine prices the board's facts. Every position of the bill of quantities is
   always in the answer: an exact material, else the nearest candidate of its catalogue group, else none (then the
   submission chooses it in the form from the requirement's attributes). Price parts that are not known count as 0;
   the total is the sum of the entered positions.
4. **Submission.** The submission agent enters the answer in the tender portal's configurator, gets the TAN from
   the webmail and signs. The materials' attributes (or the requirement's, when no material is confirmed) are given
   to it for the configurator's cascade of selections. A second attempt follows if the platform did not accept the
   bid.

There is no lead model, no recorder, no report and no hand-off between models: the board is the only connection,
and it is immediate.

## Files

| File | Role on this branch |
|---|---|
| `agent/simple.py` | Entry point (`agent.json` runs it): start, brief, one agent per website, pricing, submission |
| `agent/board.py` | The shared board: typed facts (a `facts.FactsBuilder`), a change counter, the update text for each agent (others' records plus open items), `wait`; refuses `searched_groups` from an agent that recorded no materials |
| `agent/browsing.py` | The browsing agent; board mode adds `record` (full facts schema) and `wait`, shows board updates before each step, and has no `note`, `finish` or wrap-up report |
| `agent/browser.py`, `agent/observe.js` | Page reading and actions: numbered elements, frames, dialogs first, hidden decoys dropped, paged lists, downloads; a plain page load unanswered for 25 s is requested again, a form submission is never cut short; an element named by its text is the button or link with exactly that name |
| `agent/engine/` | Deterministic pricing (rules 01–28). On this branch: every position is always bid (`allow_no_bid`, `resolve.best_candidate`), the ERP search is asked for as soon as the specification names a catalogue group, with the attributes to match |
| `agent/facts.py` | Typed facts and the update schema the agents record with |
| `agent/agent.py` | Reused for pricing and submitting (`Orchestrator.price`, `submit`, `materials`, the check against a hasty no-bid); its lead loop is not used here |
| `agent/submission.py` | The submission agent: `fill_form` (also with buttons between fields for cascades), clicks name the button pressed, a note when the same action brings it back to the same page a third time |
| `agent/llm.py` | Model client; `Model(thinking=False)` switches Qwen's thinking off |
| `agent/tests/test_simple.py` | Board and concept tests, among them two websites where the ERP agent starts the moment the specification's group is on the board |

## Settings

# Entire — talk notes and setup state (Sat 2026-10-10)

Source: Orhun's two voice recordings of the talk by Entire's CEO (ex-GitHub CEO), ~47 min in total, machine-transcribed
on-device; the raw text stays on his machine (`docs/entire-talk-transcript-raw.txt`, git-ignored). It is noisy;
points marked **(unclear)** need confirmation on Discord. CLI facts below were checked against `entire` 0.11.4 on
Orhun's machine.

## What Entire is

- A CLI that hooks into git and coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …). Every time you or the agent commits,
  the agent **session log** (prompts, responses, tool calls) is stored in the same repository as git objects and
  linked to that commit as a **checkpoint**. Checkpoints are pushed with `git push`.
- His framing: code is the most important artifact, the session log is the second. EHL makes Entire mandatory because
  the organizers want to see those session logs.
- Secrets, passwords and tokens are scrubbed from the logs, but his advice is still: never paste API tokens into the
  agent; put them in an environment variable / `.env` and let the agent read it from there.
- The company also runs a distributed git backend (regions in the US, EU/Frankfurt, Australia, India) and a web
  dashboard where sessions can be browsed, filtered to prompts only, and shared by link.

## Setup steps as demonstrated

1. Install the CLI (installer from entire.io). **Done.**
2. `entire enable` in the project folder; it can create the git repo and an initial commit, then asks which agents
   and whether to send anonymous telemetry. **Done** (all eight agents enabled, telemetry on).
3. **Codex: approve the hooks.** Codex has a trust system; on first start in the folder you must trust the folder
   and approve all seven Entire hooks, otherwise Codex sessions are not captured.
   **Not done:** `entire status` currently reports `7 Codex hook(s) need approval · open /hooks`.
4. When a session is captured the agent shows a line like "Entire will link this conversation to your next commit".
5. Create an empty repository on GitHub (he left it public), add it as `origin`, push. **Not done.**
6. Tell the agent once: "commit, and make sure the Entire session is attached". After that it remembers.
   Expected confirmation on push: `[entire] Pushing 1 checkpoint ref(s) to origin.... done` (from the Notion page).
7. On entire.io: log in with GitHub, go through onboarding, pick a region (EU), select the repository. This mirrors
   the GitHub repo to Entire and makes the sessions visible in the dashboard. **Not done.** Whether EHL requires this
   step or only steps 1–6 is **(unclear)**; the Notion page lists only install, enable and the push confirmation.
8. `entire login` in the terminal, which lets the agent search past session logs, including teammates' sessions in
   the same account/repo. He called this the last setup step. **Not done.** Related commands: `entire search`,
   `entire recap`, `entire session list`.

## Advice from the talk that matters for us

- **"Spend an hour tomorrow morning to prepare your pitch."** The jury are humans and weigh the pitch more than the
  product.
- Watch the token budget: do not burn more on API credits than the prize is worth.
- His working model: give agents tasks big enough to run unattended for a long time, with a check at the end, instead
  of many tiny supervised steps. Shared session logs are meant to stop agents repeating each other's mistakes.
- General claims (most code now written by agents, review as the new bottleneck) are opinion, not rules.

## Privacy check — before every commit and before the first push

Entire attaches the full log of every agent session registered in this folder to the next commit, and pushes it.
A session that read anything unrelated to the hackathon must not be attached.

1. `entire session list` — every listed session will be attached. Only sessions started in this folder for
   hackathon work may be there.
2. Remove any other session: `entire clean --session <id> --force`. This clears its state but **not** its data:
   also delete the shadow branch (`git branch -D entire/<base>-<hash>`; it is shared by all sessions on the same
   base commit and is rebuilt on the next turn) and the folder `.entire/metadata/<id>/`.
3. Verify what is left: `git ls-tree -r --name-only <shadow branch> | grep metadata` must list only wanted sessions.
4. A cleaned session registers again on its next turn, so close its window.

Orhun's machine.

## What Entire is

- A CLI that hooks into git and coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …). Every time you or the agent commits,
  the agent **session log** (prompts, responses, tool calls) is stored in the same repository as git objects and
  linked to that commit as a **checkpoint**. Checkpoints are pushed with `git push`.
- His framing: code is the most important artifact, the session log is the second. EHL makes Entire mandatory because
  the organizers want to see those session logs.
- Secrets, passwords and tokens are scrubbed from the logs, but his advice is still: never paste API tokens into the
  agent; put them in an environment variable / `.env` and let the agent read it from there.
- The company also runs a distributed git backend (regions in the US, EU/Frankfurt, Australia, India) and a web
  dashboard where sessions can be browsed, filtered to prompts only, and shared by link.

## Setup steps as demonstrated

1. Install the CLI (installer from entire.io). **Done.**
2. `entire enable` in the project folder; it can create the git repo and an initial commit, then asks which agents
   and whether to send anonymous telemetry. **Done** (all eight agents enabled, telemetry on).
3. **Codex: approve the hooks.** Codex has a trust system; on first start in the folder you must trust the folder
   and approve all seven Entire hooks, otherwise Codex sessions are not captured.
   **Not done:** `entire status` currently reports `7 Codex hook(s) need approval · open /hooks`.
4. When a session is captured the agent shows a line like "Entire will link this conversation to your next commit".
5. Create an empty repository on GitHub (he left it public), add it as `origin`, push. **Not done.**
6. Tell the agent once: "commit, and make sure the Entire session is attached". After that it remembers.
   Expected confirmation on push: `[entire] Pushing 1 checkpoint ref(s) to origin.... done` (from the Notion page).
7. On entire.io: log in with GitHub, go through onboarding, pick a region (EU), select the repository. This mirrors
   the GitHub repo to Entire and makes the sessions visible in the dashboard. **Not done.** Whether EHL requires this
   step or only steps 1–6 is **(unclear)**; the Notion page lists only install, enable and the push confirmation.
8. `entire login` in the terminal, which lets the agent search past session logs, including teammates' sessions in
   the same account/repo. He called this the last setup step. **Not done.** Related commands: `entire search`,
   `entire recap`, `entire session list`.

## Advice from the talk that matters for us

- **"Spend an hour tomorrow morning to prepare your pitch."** The jury are humans and weigh the pitch more than the
  product.
- Watch the token budget: do not burn more on API credits than the prize is worth.
- His working model: give agents tasks big enough to run unattended for a long time, with a check at the end, instead
  of many tiny supervised steps. Shared session logs are meant to stop agents repeating each other's mistakes.
- General claims (most code now written by agents, review as the new bottleneck) are opinion, not rules.

## Privacy check — before every commit and before the first push

Entire attaches the full log of every agent session registered in this folder to the next commit, and pushes it.
A session that read anything unrelated to the hackathon must not be attached.

1. `entire session list` — every listed session will be attached. Only sessions started in this folder for
   hackathon work may be there.
2. Remove any other session: `entire clean --session <id> --force`. This clears its state but **not** its data:
   also delete the shadow branch (`git branch -D entire/<base>-<hash>`; it is shared by all sessions on the same
   base commit and is rebuilt on the next turn) and the folder `.entire/metadata/<id>/`.
3. Verify what is left: `git ls-tree -r --name-only <shadow branch> | grep metadata` must list only wanted sessions.
4. A cleaned session registers again on its next turn, so close its window.
